Our Q4 revenue outlook reflects that shortfall in learning membership counts.

We believe that a different form factor and a significantly more interactive and visually appealing way of engaging and teaching will result in differential levels of engagement for young learners (who we believe will have a lot of fun with this experience).
Non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA loss was $5.7 million, which was better than our guidance range and represented a $4.5 million improvement from a year ago.
We expect fourth quarter revenue of $37 million to $39 million and non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA to be approximately breakeven.
We expect to end the year with $35.0 million to $37.0 million of cash, inclusive of the $30.0 million drawn on our term loan.
Based on our current operating plan, we expect existing liquidity to fund the company through free-cash-flow breakeven.

While both current year periods were impacted by a lower Active Member count when compared to the corresponding prior year periods, we expect certain product enhancements and customer acquisition initiatives that we plan to release later in the fourth quarter to support new client acquisition.

Non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA loss was $5.7 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, ahead of our guidance range of negative $9.0 million to negative $6.0 million, and compared to a non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA loss of $10.2 million in the same period in 2025.
Non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA performance relative to guidance was driven by lower sales staffing costs, lower AI costs, and disciplined G&A management.

While our Active Member count as of September 30, 2026, was lower when compared to September 30, 2025, we expect certain product enhancements and customer acquisition initiatives that we plan to release later in the fourth quarter to support new client acquisition.
These non-GAAP metrics should not be construed as an implication that our future results will be unaffected by unusual or other items.

We are not able to provide a reconciliation of non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA (loss) guidance for future periods to net loss, the comparable GAAP measure, because certain items that are excluded from non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA (loss) cannot be reasonably predicted or are not in our control.

In particular, we are unable to forecast the timing or magnitude for gains or losses on stock-based compensation without unreasonable efforts, and these items could significantly impact, either individually or in the aggregate, net income or loss in the future.
